After months of testing Liquid Glass, WhatsApp is expanding the rollout of its new iPad interface, including a brand-new Mac-style sidebar. Here's what you need to know.

WhatsApp is developing a brand-new iPad app interface

Although WhatsApp first began adapting its iOS app for the major Liquid Glass visual overhaul last October, the company didn't bring the new design to the iPad for limited testing until June this year.

At the time, WABetaInfo reported that the new design includes Liquid Glass-style tabs, buttons, and context menus, while retaining the bottom tab bar used on the iPhone.

The site's latest report notes that WhatsApp is now rolling out another major interface change to some iPad users, replacing the original bottom tab bar with a Mac-style sidebar as the default layout.

This sidebar follows the layout already used in the WhatsApp Mac version, giving users quick access to Chats, Updates, Communities, Calls, Meta AI, and other parts of the app. Users can also hide the sidebar to free up more space for the chat list and conversation view.

Here's the report:

WABetaInfo points out that the new sidebar is now available to some testers using the latest TestFlight version, but some users on the regular App Store version have also started seeing this feature.

As is common with WhatsApp's rollout approach, the new interface may take some time to reach all users, whether they're on the Beta or official version. However, iPad users will eventually benefit from a more tablet-friendly layout.
